messages:
maureen: Heads-up — noticed ~30 tiny training pods (0.5 GPU) are repeatedly landing on the same two racks in eu-west1 and getting preempted into a preempt-quarantine cycle. Node allocs stay high on those racks and overall GPU util is lumpy. Any ideas? :thinking:
josh: Seen that pattern before when NVLink lanes saturate and scheduler prefers low-latency co-location. Which pools are these on?
maureen: pool=eu-west1-gpu-small, taints look normal. Grafana shows NVLink errors + pod preempt events spiking at 09:12 UTC: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/cluster/eu-west1-gpu?orgId=1&refresh=5s
sylvia: SRE alert kicked in: sre-bot: GPU thermal / nvlink errors on rack-r12 and rack-r13, auto-drain started 09:15. That explains the preempts. But why are small pods all concentrated there?
oliver: Could be scheduler affinity bucketing — recent cfg change set rackWeight to prefer racks with low cpu pressure; those racks were tagged as "fast-network" so tiny pods gravitated.
josh: Reminder: small-pod gang coalescing was enabled in the last rollout (ramp 50%). It groups tiny pods to reduce NVLink context switching; but if one rack gets sticky, eviction ripple happens.
maureen: kubectl get pods -o wide | grep preempt
```
NAME                             READY   STATUS            NODE           AGE
trainer-small-5c9b8             0/1     Preempted         rack-r12-node3 5m
trainer-small-9bf4a             0/1     Preempted         rack-r12-node7 4m
trainer-small-2e3d1             0/1     Preempt-quarantine rack-r13-node4 3m
```
josh: Thanks — that quarantine state is the scheduler's temporary hold when preempted repeatedly. It prevents thrash but can block backlog. Two options: 1) widen placement diversity for small pods (disable strict rack affinity), 2) temporarily scale up small pool across more racks.
sylvia: Cost note: this thrash bumped short-term GPU hours by ~18% for that queue yesterday, so scaling blindly has cost impact. We should prefer a placement fix.
oliver: Quick rollback we can do: revert rackWeight change for small-pod profiles to previous default (rollout id: rollout/2026-03-14-rack-pref). That should spread placement. I can cut a canary in 10m.
sre-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-1953 — NVLink errors on rack-r12/r13. Assigned to @oliver and @infra-oncall.
maureen: If we revert rackWeight, any extra preemptions expected while scheduler rebalances?
josh: Minimal — scheduler will spread new pods across racks; existing quarantined pods remain until they retry/expire. Consider manual eviction of a couple stuck pods to force reschedule if needed.
sylvia: Also propose adding a safety: if preempt rate > 5/min on a rack, set >rack-quarantine-flag so scheduler avoids placing new small pods there for 15m. Low-effort guardrail.
oliver: Agree, we'll add that to the scheduler's placement policy as a short-term tweak. I'll open an RFC for the quarantine-avoid rule and cut the rackWeight revert now.
maureen: Thanks. Cutting revert now and watching. Will post updates. :thumbsup:
scheduler-bot: Robo-scheduler: rollout rollback queued: rollout/2026-03-14-rack-pref -> paused for canary 2/10 nodes; monitoring placements.
maureen: update 09:40 UTC — placements have started spreading, preempt events down ~70%, NVLink errors still being triaged by infra-oncall. If things look stable will close incident.
